data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The claim that decentralization provides superior correlated-failure resilience is unfalsifiable as typically stated, because 'independence' is defined post-hoc: any observed systemic failure in a decentralized network retroactively redefines previously 'independent' nodes as having shared a hidden common cause, making the hypothesis immune to refutation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A formal, pre-registered metric for independence exists that does not rely on enumerating shared causes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Failures in decentralized networks are consistently attributed to local, node-specific causes rather than systemic correlations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The definition of independence can be operationalized without reference to shared causes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If we treat independence as the absence of shared causes, we cannot test it without enumerating all possible shared causes. When a decentralized network survives a shock, it is cited as evidence of independence; when it fails, the failure is explained away as a newly discovered correlation.
